title: Recipes from the River: Chopped Red Cabbage & Dill Slaw
contentHtml:
This chopped red cabbage slaw comes together quickly using pantry staples. It's a pretty big dill.

If you've been paying attention to this series sharing our recipes from the Moab Music Festival (see the full Cooking on the River series here), you may have noticed a trend for each night's menu: Heavy, hearty, rich main course + Light, tangy side salads.

... And we're not here to argue with what works!

Having a variety of side salads at your disposal helps you get some varied veg into your diet and keeps your plates interesting. It was also particularly helpful for meal planning when we only had a few coolers at our disposal for the duration of our trip.

We served this Chopped Red Cabbage Slaw on the third and final night of our journey alongside Oklahoma Onion Burgers (recipe coming tomorrow) and an in-the-moment take on this Japanese Potato Salad with our leftover ingredients.

Every recipe I publish here is personally tested, tasted, and approved.

Serves: 6

Ingredients

  • 1 small head of red cabbage, finely shredded or chopped

  • ½ large sweet onion, very thinly sliced

  • 1 bunch fresh dill, roughly chopped cup cider vinegar

  • ¼ cup granulated sugar

  • ¼ cup neutral oil

  • 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard

  • Kosher salt

  • Freshly ground black pepper

Method

  1. Make the dressing. Whisk together cider vinegar, sugar, oil, and Dijon until the sugar is dissolved and the dressing is emulsified. Season with salt and pepper.

  2. Toss together. Combine cabbage and onion in a large bowl. Add the dressing and toss thoroughly to coat.

  3. Rest. Let stand for 20 to 30 minutes, tossing once or twice, until the cabbage has softened slightly but retains plenty of crunch.

  4. Garnish and serve. Fold in the dill immediately before serving. Taste and adjust with additional salt, pepper, or cider vinegar as needed.
